stem:
Qasim adds the scores $3$, $8$, $5$, $2$, and $7$ from five short games. He wants the parity of the total without adding all the values.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The answer is the word odd, because odd is the label that belongs on any parity question.
The total is even, because even scores appear in the list.
The total is odd, because there are three odd addends.
He should split the scores into short and long rhythms instead of counting odd addends.

teacher.key_rationale: Even addends do not change parity. Three odd addends make an odd sum, so the total is odd.
